The test image shows a **leaf** with numerous small to medium dark brown/black spots scattered across a yellowing leaf surface. Some spots coalesce into larger necrotic areas. No concentric rings or fuzzy growth visible.

Leaf candidates (13 classes). My top suspects based on symptoms:
1. **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato** - small black spots with yellow halos
2. **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** - small circular tan/gray lesions
3. **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** - bronzing with necrotic spots
4. **Early_Blight** - larger dark spots with concentric rings

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Bacterial Speck reference shows fewer, more isolated dark spots on a green leaf. The test image has far more spots and much more yellowing. Not a great match. Let me check Septoria.

Septoria reference shows a yellowed leaf with numerous small dark spots - quite similar to the test image in terms of the yellowing and spot density. Good match. Let me check Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus next.
TSWV reference shows bronzing with purplish scattered spots - different color pattern from the test image. Less of a match. Let me check Early Blight.
Early Blight shows larger, fewer dark brown lesions with yellowing - spots are much bigger than in the test image. Not a close match. Let me check 4 more classes.
That's a microscope image, not useful for comparison. Let me continue with other candidates.
Bacterial Canker shows marginal leaf scorching, very different from the test image's scattered spots. Not a match.
Verticillium Wilt shows wilting/drooping leaves, no spots. Not a match. One view remaining - let me check Leaf Mold as my 8th class.

Leaf Mold shows velvety texture, not distinct spots. Poor match.

| Early_Blight | Poor - larger, fewer lesions |
| Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus | Poor - bronzing/purplish color, different pattern |
| Late_Blight | N/A - microscope image |
| Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato | Poor - marginal scorching pattern |
| Verticillium_Wilt | Poor - wilting, no spots |
| Leaf_Mold | Poor - velvety mold, no distinct spots |

The test image shows a heavily yellowed leaf covered with numerous small dark brown spots that coalesce in places. This matches Septoria Leaf Blotch: small lesions (< 1/8 inch), no concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight), dense spotting causing leaf blight, and overall yellowing. The Septoria reference image showed a strikingly similar pattern.
